# MCP & WebMCP Tools

> Complete schema, scope, OAuth discovery, elicitation, and JSON-RPC error reference for DakFlare's 9 Streamable HTTP MCP tools and 4 browser WebMCP tools.

## Streamable HTTP MCP Server (`/mcp`)

- **Endpoints**: `POST /mcp` (JSON-RPC requests & batches), `GET /mcp` (SSE stream for stateful sessions), `DELETE /mcp` (terminate session). Legacy `POST /v1/mcp` remains supported for stateless `_meta` clients.
- **Required Header**: `Accept` must include `application/json` or `text/event-stream` (otherwise HTTP `406`).
- **Session Tracking**: Stateful clients track `Mcp-Session-Id`; stateless clients pass `params._meta`.
- **OAuth Discovery (Public)**:
  - `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` (RFC 9728)
  - `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414)
  - Audience binding enforced per RFC 8707; `401` responses include `WWW-Authenticate` pointing to the metadata document.
- **Stdio Bridge**: `dakflare mcp serve --token-file <path>`

> **Contract Drift Note**: `worker/src/mcp/tools.ts` currently registers **9 tools** (including `triage` and `telemetry`), whereas `contracts/mcp-tools.json` reflects the earlier 7-tool snapshot. Run `node worker/scripts/mcp-contract.mjs --write` to regenerate `contracts/mcp-tools.json`.

## The 9 MCP Tools (`worker/src/mcp/tools.ts`)

`tools/list` filters dynamically by the caller's token scopes. Calling an unregistered tool returns JSON-RPC `-32601`.

| Tool | Required Scope | Inputs | Output Summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_devices` | `devices:read` | `{ archived?: boolean }` | `{ devices: [{ device_id, label, sim_slot, last_seen, fcm }] }` |
| `read_messages` | `messages:read` | `{ device_id (Mcp-Param-Device-Id), limit?: 1..200 }` | `{ messages: [{ id, local_id, direction, peer, body, received_at, reply_verdict }], limit }` |
| `command_status` | `messages:read` | `{ command_id, device_id }` | `{ command: { command_id, state, to? } \| null }` |
| `list_flows` | `flows:read` | `{}` | `{ workflows: [{ id, name, enabled, node_count }] }` |
| `get_flow` | `flows:read` | `{ id }` | `{ workflow: { id, name, version, graph } \| null }` |
| `triage` | `messages:read` | `{ message (1..4096), sender (1..64), spans?: [{ index, text }] (max 20) }` | `{ intent, injection, specificity, roles, invariant: { balanceAtLeastPrincipal }, source }` |
| `telemetry` | `devices:read` | `{ question (1..500) }` | `{ plan, rows, truncated, took_ms }` |
| `trace` | `messages:read` | `{ id, device_id? }` | `{ verdict, kind, why: string[] }` |
| `send_sms` | `sms:send` (+ grant) | `{ device_id, to (E.164), body (<=4096), idempotency_key? (<=128) }` | `{ command_id?, sent, approval_request_id? }` or MRTR `input_required` |

> **Header Binding (`x-mcp-header`)**: `read_messages.device_id` declares `x-mcp-header: "Device-Id"`, mapped to request header `Mcp-Param-Device-Id`. A header/argument mismatch returns JSON-RPC `-32020`.

## Elicitation & Multi-Round-Trip (`send_sms`)

Mutating tools never execute on an unapproved agent token:
1. If no live `sms:send:production` grant covers the target, `send_sms` returns an MCP `input_required` result (or SSE `elicitation/create` prompt requiring `confirm_deployment`, 6-digit `totp_code`, and `max_uses`).
2. Grants minted via elicitation are clamped by `SCOPE_CAPS` and capped at 15 minutes.
3. On retry, the tool re-reads the authority store in D1/`AuthorityGuard`; client-supplied `inputResponses` can never widen permissions.

## JSON-RPC Error Codes

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `-32700` | Parse error |
| `-32600` | Invalid JSON-RPC envelope or session |
| `-32601` | Unknown or out-of-scope tool |
| `-32602` | Invalid params, or payload mutated after confirmation |
| `-32603` | Internal server error |
| `-32000` | Not acceptable (`Accept` header missing JSON/SSE) |
| `-32001` | Session not found |
| `-32002` | Elicitation declined by operator |
| `-32003` | Elicitation timed out |
| `-32004` | TOTP code rejected |
| `-32020` | `Mcp-Param-*` header mismatch |

## Browser WebMCP Tools (`/admin/workflows/edit`)

Registered on `document.modelContext` (fallback `navigator.modelContext`) while the workflow editor is mounted:

| Tool | Annotations | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dakflare_get_flow_ast` | `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false` | Returns live `{ flow_id, name, enabled, dirty, staged_patch, graph }` |
| `dakflare_stage_flow_patch` | `readOnlyHint: false`, `consequentialHint: true`, `destructiveHint: true` | Validates and stages a dashed ghost preview (`STAGED PATCH · NOT APPLIED`); never saves |
| `dakflare_synthesize_pattern` | `destructiveHint: false` | Runs local `flow.wasm` template synthesis from `sample` and optional `spans` |
| `dakflare_diagnose_message` | `readOnlyHint: true`, `destructiveHint: false` | Calls `POST /v1/agent/diagnose` with a 15s timeout |

---

<!-- source: /docs/reference/wasm-flow-abi.md -->

# Wasm Flow ABI & IR v2

> Hand-rolled WebAssembly C ABI for simulator/flow-wasm and complete dakflare.flow/v2 intermediate representation specification.

DakFlare compiles its pure-Rust flow engine (`simulator/flow`) to `wasm32-unknown-unknown` (`simulator/flow-wasm/build.sh` → `worker/src/wasm/flow.wasm` and `dashboard/static/flow.wasm`) without `wasm-bindgen`, so Cloudflare Workers can instantiate the module synchronously with zero loader glue.

## Binary Framing Contract

Every call passes UTF-8 JSON into linear memory and returns a pointer to a length-prefixed frame:

```text
[ 4 bytes: u32 little-endian payload length ][ payload UTF-8 JSON bytes ]
```

**Critical safety rule**: Always construct fresh `DataView` / `Uint8Array` views over `wasm.memory.buffer` *after* calling any exported function—allocation inside Wasm can grow linear memory and detach previously captured ArrayBuffer views. Always call `dealloc(outPtr, 4 + length)` and `dealloc(inputPtr, inputLen)` to free both buffers.

## Exported C ABI Functions (`simulator/flow-wasm/src/lib.rs`)

| Export | Signature | Input JSON | Output JSON |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `alloc` | `(len: usize) -> *mut u8` | — | Allocates `len` bytes in Wasm memory |
| `dealloc` | `(ptr: *mut u8, len: usize) -> void` | — | Frees a buffer returned by `alloc` or a `*_json` function |
| `run_json` | `(ptr, len) -> *mut u8` | `{ graph, message: { sender, body, received_at } }` | `FlowResult`: `{ matched, outcome, actions, variables, steps, error? }` |
| `validate_json` | `(ptr, len) -> *mut u8` | Raw flow graph object | `{ ok: true, graph }` (stamped with `schema` & `rank-v1` `ui_layout`) or `{ ok: false, issues }` |
| `layout_json` | `(ptr, len) -> *mut u8` | Raw flow graph object | `{ ok: true, algorithm: "rank-v1", positions: { [id]: { x, y } } }` |
| `trace_json` | `(ptr, len) -> *mut u8` | `{ graph, message }` | Validates then runs: `{ ok: true, trace: FlowResult }` or `{ ok: false, issues }` |
| `synthesize_json` | `(ptr, len) -> *mut u8` | `{ samples: [{ body, value }], negatives?: string[], group?: string }` | `{ ok: true, result: { pattern, group, precision, recall, ... } }` or `{ ok: false, reason, message }` |
| `synthesize_template_json` | `(ptr, len) -> *mut u8` | `{ sample_body, spans: TemplateSpan[], additional_samples? }` | `{ ok: true, result: { pattern, trigger_phrases, variables, test_results } }` |
| `suggest_spans_json` | `(ptr, len) -> *mut u8` | `{ body: string }` | `{ ok: true, spans: TemplateSpan[] }` |

## Canonical Flow IR (`dakflare.flow/v2`)

Derived from `cli/schema/flow-v2.json` and `worker/src/lib/flow-ir.ts`:

### Node Kinds (9 Total)

| `type` | Required `data` Fields | Outgoing `sourceHandle` Rules |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger` | `kind: "incoming"`, optional `sender: { mode: any\|exact\|prefix\|regex, value? }`, `body: { mode: any\|keyword\|regex, value? }` | 1 unlabelled edge; binds `sender`, `body`, `received_at` |
| `extract` | `pattern` (RE2, 1–512 chars, ≥1 `(?<name>...)` group), optional `source: "body"\|"sender"`, `flags: ""\|"i"` | 1 unlabelled edge; binds named capture groups |
| `set_var` | `name` (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,31}$`, not builtin), `value` (template ≤2048 chars) | 1 unlabelled edge |
| `condition` | `left` (template), `op: equals\|not_equals\|contains\|matches\|exists`, `right?` (required unless `exists`) | 2 edges: `true` and `false` |
| `switch` | `value` (template), `cases: string[]` (1–8 items) | `case:0` .. `case:<n-1>` plus `default` |
| `delay` | `seconds` (integer `1..300`) | 1 unlabelled edge (>5s runs in `FlowExecutionWorkflow`) |
| `webhook` | `url` (`^https://`, SSRF-checked: no loopback/private/CGNAT/metadata), optional `body` template | 1 unlabelled edge (dispatched via `WEBHOOK_QUEUE`) |
| `send_sms` | `to` (1–32 chars), `body` (1–4096 chars) | 1 unlabelled edge |
| `stop` | `{ reason?: string }` | 0 outgoing edges |

### Structural Limits

| Constraint | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Max nodes (`flow-v2.json` / `config.ts`) | 200 in IR schema (50 in legacy `MAX_WORKFLOW_NODES` guard) |
| Max edges (`flow-v2.json` / `config.ts`) | 400 in IR schema (100 in legacy `MAX_WORKFLOW_EDGES` guard) |
| Max graph serialized size | 65,536 bytes (`MAX_WORKFLOW_GRAPH_BYTES`) |
| Node / edge ID pattern | `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` |
| Variable template syntax | `{{ name }}` or `{{ vars.name }}` (must be bound on every incoming path) |
| Topology | Strictly acyclic DAG; cycles rejected with offending edge |

<!-- source: /docs/reference/cli-and-env.md -->

# CLI, Bindings & Error Codes

> Reference for all 33 dakflare CLI commands, semantic exit codes, Cloudflare bindings, environment variables, secrets, and the 17-code §8 error catalog.

## `dakflare` CLI Machine Contract

- Zero npm dependencies. The release binaries need no Node; `cf` and a source checkout do. Config is stored at `~/.config/dakflare/config.json` (mode `600`).
- `--agent` (or `--json`): emits one compact JSON document per invocation, never prompts, never emits ANSI colors.
- Pass `--yes` on destructive or interactive commands in automation.

### Semantic Exit Codes

| Exit Code | Meaning | Agent Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Success | Proceed |
| `1` | Failed check or terminal error (`FAILED`, `EXPIRED`) | Inspect `error` payload |
| `2` | Usage error or invalid schema (`workflow_invalid`) | Fix flags or document |
| `3` | Resource not found | Verify ID with `devices` / `list_flows` |
| `4` | Permission denied (`401` / `403`) | Check token scopes or human credential |
| `5` | Conflict (`version_conflict`, `409` approval race) | Re-read state before retrying |
| `6` | Precondition failed (`approval_required`, `agent_quota_exceeded`, `heal_refused`) | Obtain approval or fix corpus regression |
| `75` | Temporary / still in flight (`send` poll timeout, network) | **Never re-run `send`**; poll `dakflare status <command_id>` |

### Command Inventory (33 Commands)

- **Provision**: `setup`, `init`, `up`, `doctor`, `pair`, `devices`, `revoke`
- **Messaging**: `send` (SMS, or `--channel --connector` for a platform), `status`, `audit`
- **Templates & audience**: `templates list`, `templates create`, `templates delete`, `contacts import`
- **Scheduling**: `schedule list`, `schedule create`, `schedule cancel`
- **Channels**: `connectors list`, `connectors create`, `connectors update`, `connectors delete`, `webhooks list`, `webhooks create`, `webhooks delete`, `webhooks deliveries`
- **Auth & Control Plane**: `auth bootstrap`, `auth invite`, `auth invites`, `auth reset`, `auth mint-agent-token`, `auth agent-tokens`, `auth revoke-agent-token`, `auth approvals`, `auth approve`, `auth reject`, `auth grants`, `auth grants revoke`
- **Automation**: `flows apply`, `flows heal`, `rules list`, `rules apply`, `rules update`, `rules delete`, `rules test`, `extract synthesize`
- **Agent Work**: `ai` (`ai providers`, `ai configure`, `ai models`, `ai test`), `ask`, `fix`, `flow test`, `flow apply`, `schema --flow-v2`
- **Provenance**: `trace`, `alerts`, `dlq`, `ws inspect`
- **Contract**: `capabilities`, `describe`, `schema` (`schema states`), `examples`, `mcp serve`, `key fingerprint`

`dakflare setup` is the interactive first-run path: it checks Node, npm, git, `cf` and `gh`,
prepares the Worker pack or source dependencies, writes the local secrets, offers to star the
repository, and can run `up`. `--yes` never stars or deploys without `--star`/`--deploy`.

`--pack <dir>` uses a precompiled release pack (a Cloudflare Build Output v1 plus migrations and
`pack.json`); `up --pack` fills its D1/KV ids and runs `cf deploy --prebuilt`, with no npm install
or console build. `--checkout` forces the source path. The release binaries and pack are described
in `docs/RELEASE.md`.

## Cloudflare Bindings (`worker/cloudflare.config.ts` & `worker/wrangler.toml`)

| Binding | Type | Resource / Class |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DB` | D1 Database | `sms_gateway` (19 migrations: `0001`–`0019`) |
| `KV` | KV Namespace | FCM HTTP v1 bearer-token cache |
| `MEDIA_BUCKET` | R2 Bucket | `dakflare-media` (24h `agent_attachments` storage) |
| `DEVICE` | Durable Object (SQLite) | `DeviceGateway` |
| `AUTH_GUARD` | Durable Object (SQLite) | `AuthGuard` |
| `AUTHORITY_GUARD` | Durable Object (SQLite) | `AuthorityGuard` |
| `ASSISTANT` | Durable Object (SQLite) | `AssistantAgent` |
| `CHANNEL_CONN` | Durable Object (SQLite) | `ChannelConnection` (one object per `channel:account_id`) |
| `SCHEDULER` | Durable Object (SQLite) | `Scheduler` (single `scheduler` instance: due rows, token buckets, quiet hours) |
| `WEBHOOK_QUEUE` | Queue (producer & consumer) | `dakflare-webhook-queue` (`max_batch_size=10`, `max_retries=3`) |
| `INGEST_QUEUE` | Queue (producer & consumer) | `dakflare-ingest-queue` (`max_batch_size=50`, `max_batch_timeout=2`, DLQ `dakflare-ingest-dlq`) |
| `FLOW_WORKFLOW` | Workflow | `FlowExecutionWorkflow` (`flow-execution-workflow`) |
| `AI` | Workers AI | Clef System 1 & optional chat provider |
| Rate Limiters | 7 namespaces (`1001`–`1007`) | `PAIR_LIMITER` (30/60s), `ADMIN_LIMITER` (600/60s), `DEVICE_LIMITER` (600/60s), `AUTH_FAIL_LIMITER` (120/60s), `PAIR_GLOBAL_LIMITER` (300/60s), `AUTH_ACCOUNT_LIMITER` (5/60s), `AUTH_IP_LIMITER` (20/60s) |

## Environment Variables & Secrets

### Secrets (Set via `cf workers secrets update`, Never in `wrangler.toml`)

- `ADMIN_TOKEN` — required; admin routes fail closed with `401` when unset
- `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` — signs session cookies & encrypts TOTP secrets (absent → `/api/auth` & `/v1/auth/*` return `503`)
- `AUTH_PEPPER` — `v2:<b64 32B>,v1:<b64 32B>`
- `RESEND_API_KEY` — optional; enables magic-link sign-in door
- `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` — optional; enables FCM HTTP v1 wake pushes
- `AI_PROVIDER_API_KEY` (fallbacks: `AI_CHAT_API_KEY`, `TOKENLAB_API_KEY`) — optional external AI gateway key
- `WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY` — AES-256-GCM key sealing inbound webhook secrets

### Key `[vars]` Defaults

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENT_RUNTIME` | `"on"` | `"on"` enables `AssistantAgent`; `"off"` returns `503` on `/agents/*` |
| `BINDING_AUTH` | `"trusted"` | `DakFlareApi` service binding auth: `"trusted"` or `"agent_token"` |
| `AUTH_PASSWORD_MODE` | `"client-derived"` | `"off"`, `"client-derived"` (browser PBKDF2), or `"server-kdf"` (paid tier) |
| `AUTH_LOCKOUT_WINDOW_SECONDS` | `"900"` | Lockout window in `AuthGuard` |
| `MAGIC_LINK_TTL_SECONDS` | `"900"` | Single-use magic link expiry |
| `MESSAGE_RETENTION_DAYS` | `"90"` | Daily cron (`17 3 * * *`) retention cutoff |
| `INCOMING_ROWS_PER_DAY` | `"10000"` | Per-device daily inbound write quota |
| `AI_DAILY_TOKEN_BUDGET` | `"20000"` | Daily token budget for stateless console assistant |

`LEASE_MS`, `ACK_TIMEOUT_MS`, `OFFLINE_ALERT_MS`, `STALE_SOCKET_MS`, and `NONCE_WINDOW_MS` are **not declared in any config carrier** — no `[vars]` block sets them. They are code defaults in `worker/src/lib/config.ts` (60 s lease, 8 s ack, 15 min offline alert, 2 min stale socket, 5 min P-256 replay window). A deployment overrides one only by adding the variable itself.

## Uniform §8 Error Code Catalog (`worker/src/lib/errors.ts`)

| Error Code | HTTP | Meaning & Recovery |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `unexpected_query` | `400` | Signed device route received a query string; strip query params |
| `bad_request` | `400` | Malformed JSON or missing required field |
| `rule_rejected` | `400` | Rule failed flow-graph compilation |
| `workflow_invalid` | `400` | Admin-only; includes `details: [{ path, message }]` |
| `idempotency_key_not_supported_in_batch` | `400` | Do not send `idempotency_key` to `/v1/sms/send/batch` |
| `missing_auth_headers` | `401` | One or more of `X-Device-Id`, `X-Timestamp`, `X-Nonce`, `X-Signature` missing |
| `malformed_header` | `401` | Header failed regex validation |
| `timestamp_out_of_window` | `401` | `X-Timestamp` outside ±300,000 ms; sync handset clock |
| `bad_signature_length` | `401` | Decoded `X-Signature` is not 64 bytes (IEEE P1363 `r \|\| s`) |
| `invalid_signature` | `401` | ECDSA verification failed against stored P-256 public key |
| `device_unknown` | `401` | `device_id` not registered or revoked |
| `nonce_replay` | `401` | `X-Nonce` already spent within `NONCE_WINDOW_MS`; generate a new 16-byte nonce |
| `device_exists` | `409` | Pairing attempted unauthorized rebind of an active `device_id` |
| `payload_too_large` | `413` | Body exceeded `MAX_BODY_BYTES` (262,144 bytes) |
| `rate_limited` | `429` | Rate limiter bucket exhausted; back off |
| `daily_quota_exceeded` | `429` | Device exhausted `INCOMING_ROWS_PER_DAY`; retry tomorrow |
| `storage_unavailable` | `503` | Backing D1/DO write failed; batch was NOT written—safe to retry |

<!-- source: /docs/reference/state-machines.md -->

# State Machines

> Authoritative inventory of DakFlare's guarded, declared, and derived state machines across outbound commands, replies, approvals, grants, agent turns, and auth.

Every state machine in DakFlare is classified by how its transitions are enforced:
- **Guarded**: One atomic SQL predicate or function owns the transition; no route can bypass it.
- **Declared**: Schema enumerates valid states, but enforcement lives in route predicates or lacks a writer.
- **Derived**: Computed dynamically from timestamps and counters at read time.

## Outbound Command Delivery (**Guarded**)

Owned by `worker/src/durable-object.ts` (`ALLOWED_PREDECESSORS`):

```text
PENDING -> LEASED -> DISPATCHED -> SENT -> DELIVERED
                         |            |
                         +-----------> FAILED (with optional error_code & error_message)
PENDING | LEASED | DISPATCHED -> EXPIRED (error_code: "expired")
```

- **Terminal states**: `DELIVERED`, `FAILED`, `EXPIRED` (no transition ever leaves them).
- **Out-of-order safety**: `DELIVERED` accepts `DISPATCHED` as well as `SENT` because carrier delivery reports can arrive before radio ack; late `SENT` after `DELIVERED` is a no-op; `LEASED` cannot jump directly to `DELIVERED`.
- **Canonical lifecycle projection** (`worker/src/lib/canonical-lifecycle.ts`, **Derived**): maps raw state into `(state, substate, is_terminal, settled, remediation)` including `SETTLED_SENT` after 5 minutes of silence (`SMS_SETTLED_GRACE_MS`).

## Inbound Reply Fate (**Guarded**)

Owned by `worker/src/routes/incoming.ts`:
- **States**: `null` → any valid state (`queued`, `sent`, `delivered`, `failed`); then `queued` → `sent` → `delivered` / `failed`. `delivered` and `failed` are terminal.
- **Suppression axis (`reply_verdict`)**: `suppressed_cooldown` or `suppressed_hourly_cap` (`0004_provenance.sql`).

## Flow Run (**Guarded on Handset & Worker**)

- **States**: `delivered`, `partial`, `halted`, `filtered`, `no_trigger`, `error`.
- When the handset encounters a `delay` or `webhook` node it cannot execute locally, it marks the run `partial` (`simulator/core/src/carrier.rs`). The Worker skips SMS steps already executed before the boundary and resumes the remaining actions (`worker/src/flow/dispatch.ts`).

## Authority, Autonomy & Agent Runtime

| Machine | States | Enforcement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Approval Request** | `PENDING` → `APPROVED` / `REJECTED` / `EXPIRED` / `CANCELLED` | **Declared** (`0003` CHECK + atomic single-winner claim; loser gets `409`) |
| **Authority Grant** | `live` → `revoked` / `expired` / `exhausted` | **Derived** (`agent/grants.ts`; note: all three non-live endings currently surface as `grant_expired`) |
| **Autonomy Window** | `off`, `open`, `expired`, `other-session` | **Derived** on every act; ordered refusals: `webhook_cannot_act`, `autonomy_off`, `autonomy_other_session`, `autonomy_expired`, `sms_cap`/`write_cap`, `daily_sms_cap`, `no_grant`, `grant_expired` |
| **Runtime WS Ticket** | `issued` → `spent` / `expired` | **Guarded** (atomic conditional `DELETE ... WHERE expires_at > ?` in `lib/agent-runtime.ts`) |
| **Assistant Proposal** | `pending` → `consumed` / `expired` | **Guarded** (conditional claim before effect; duplicate click gets `409 already_applied`; failed effect releases claim) |
| **Agent Turn** | `running` → `done` / `failed` | **Guarded** for completed replay (`<key>:answer` returns `replayed: true`) |
| **Scheduled DO Work** | no state column — `run_at` plus `attempts`; an alarm returns `consumed` / `rescheduled` (`TaskOutcome`), and after 5 attempts the row is moved to the separate `dead_letters` table | **Guarded** (`durable-object.ts`) |
| **Auth Lockout** | `ok` → `counting` → `locked` | **Guarded** across two scopes in `AuthGuard`: per-account (5) and per-IP (20) |

## Known Unwritten / Declared-Only Columns

- `device_sims.radio_state` (`READY`, `DEGRADED`, `NO_SERVICE`, `LOCKED`): declared in `0002`, read by telemetry, no handset writer yet.
- `conversations.session_state` (`NO_SESSION`, `WINDOW_OPEN`, `TEMPLATE_ONLY`, `OPTED_OUT`): Telegram and WhatsApp inserts currently hard-code `WINDOW_OPEN`.
- `alerts` (`extraction_drift`): `device_offline` auto-resolves on handset contact; drift alerts do not auto-resolve yet.

<!-- source: /docs/reference/glossary.md -->

# Canonical Glossary

> Locked canonical identifiers and nouns across DakFlare's codebase, API, CLI, and documentation to prevent terminology drift.

Use these exact identifiers across code, API payloads, CLI flags, prompts, and documentation. Never substitute synonyms.

| Canonical Term | Exact Definition | Never Call This |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `device_id` | Paired handset identifier (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$`, e.g. `dev63f3953f417d587f`) | `handsetId`, `phone_id`, `radio_node_id` |
| `command_id` | Outbound SMS command identifier returned by `POST /v1/sms/send` (e.g. `cmdf_...`) | `job_id`, `sms_id`, `message_job` |
| `local_id` | Handset-assigned idempotency key for an inbound SMS row | `sms_local_key`, `phone_msg_id` |
| `dkf_agt_` | Prefix for scoped agent bearer tokens (SHA-256 digest stored in D1 `agent_tokens`) | `api_key`, `bot_token`, `service_token` |
| `ag1_` | Prefix for single-use authority apply handles minted by `POST /v1/agent/synthesize` | `patch_token`, `deploy_key` |
| `DeviceGateway` | Per-handset SQLite Durable Object (`DEVICE` binding) | `HandsetDO`, `SmsRouterDO` |
| `AuthGuard` | Global SQLite Durable Object (`AUTH_GUARD`) owning per-account & per-IP lockouts | `RateLimitDO`, `LoginGuard` |
| `AuthorityGuard` | Global SQLite Durable Object (`AUTHORITY_GUARD`) owning live grant windows | `GrantDO`, `ApprovalDO` |
| `AssistantAgent` | Pinned singleton SQLite Durable Object (`ASSISTANT`, name `assistant`) for the stateful agent runtime | `ChatDO`, `AgentSessionDO` |
| `FlowExecutionWorkflow` | Cloudflare Workflow (`FLOW_WORKFLOW`) executing flow delays >5 seconds | `DelayWorker`, `FlowQueue` |
| `DakFlareApi` | Typed Cloudflare Worker-to-Worker RPC service binding entrypoint (`worker/src/binding-api.ts`) | `InternalApi`, `WorkerRpc` |
| `dakflare.flow/v2` | Canonical acyclic flow IR schema (`cli/schema/flow-v2.json`) | `flow-v1`, `canvas-json`, `plugin-manifest` |
| `SENT` vs. `DELIVERED` | `SENT` = handset radio accepted the message; `DELIVERED` = carrier status report confirmed arrival | Treating `SENT` as delivered |
| `poll-only` | Handset wake mode when `fcm_token` is absent (GMS-free LineageOS); polls `/v1/sms/outgoing/poll` | `broken push`, `offline-only` |
| `System 1` / `Clef` | Typed probability-over-closed-set decision client (`worker/src/lib/system1.ts`) | Free-form LLM classifier |

<!-- source: /docs/architecture/sovereign-edge-model.md -->

# Sovereign Edge Model

> Architectural rationale for pairing a dedicated Android handset radio with a single-tenant Cloudflare Worker instead of third-party telecom SaaS.

DakFlare is built around one thesis: **the handset is the radio, the Worker is the coordinator, and the operator owns both.**

## Why Handset + Cloudflare Edge

1. **Zero Telecom SaaS Markup or Account Lock-In**: Standard SMS APIs charge per-segment markups, enforce rigid sender-ID approval pipelines, and store your private message traffic on third-party servers. Running a dedicated Android handset on your own SIM eliminates per-message intermediaries while keeping local carrier reachability.
2. **Offline-First Automation**: Because the Rust `simulator/flow` interpreter runs natively on the handset, simple auto-reply graphs execute even when cellular data or edge connectivity drops—and synchronize provenance back to D1 once connectivity returns.
3. **Single-Tenant Edge Scalability**: Running the coordinator on your own Cloudflare account gives global TLS termination, hibernating WebSockets (`DeviceGateway`), SQLite Durable Objects, D1 (`sms_gateway`), Queues (`WEBHOOK_QUEUE`), and Workflows (`FlowExecutionWorkflow`) at pennies per month—while keeping credentials strictly on the operator's machine (zero Cloudflare tokens in CI).

## Repository & Data Architecture

- **`worker/`**: TypeScript Cloudflare Worker (`dakflare-worker`), 19 D1 migrations (`0001_baseline.sql`–`0019_templates_and_scheduling.sql`), 6 SQLite Durable Objects, 5 channel adapters (SMS, Telegram, WhatsApp Cloud, Messenger, Instagram), `flow.wasm`, Clef System 1, and `/mcp`.
- **`simulator/`**: Tauri v2 + Rust `core/` + Rust `flow/` + `flow-wasm/` + Kotlin telephony bridge (`SmsReceiver`, `SmsSender`, `SmsProvider`, `GatewayService`, `BootReceiver`, `KeyVault`) + Svelte 5 SPA.
- **`dashboard/`**: Svelte 5 with SvelteKit static console (`adapter-static` → `worker/public/admin`), container-query responsive tables (measured at 390–1440 px), Svelte Flow editor with WebMCP, and floating Assistant.
- **`cli/`**: Zero-dependency Node 22+ `dakflare` CLI (33 commands).

## Honest Architectural Boundaries (Known Gaps)

- **MMS** is not supported (surfaces an explicit notification instead of dropping silently).
- **Plugin registry & arbitrary third-party Wasm plugins**: Schema tables (`plugin_repos`, `installed_plugins`) exist from migration `0007`, but only the first-party compiled `flow.wasm` interpreter runs today.
- **`server-kdf` password mode** requires Cloudflare Workers Paid tier (server-side PBKDF2 exceeds the 10 ms Free-tier CPU budget; `client-derived` is the default).
- **Revoked devices are tombstones**: `DELETE /v1/admin/devices/:id` sets `revoked_at` and strips credentials while preserving message history; re-pairing the same `device_id` revives the row.

---

<!-- source: /docs/architecture/security-p256-identity.md -->

# P-256 Identity & Authentication

> Hardware-wrapped P-256 device signing, canonical string construction, replay protection, and Better Auth multi-factor operator security.

## Zero Shared Secrets Between Handset and Edge

Every device request is authenticated with asymmetric **ECDSA P-256** (`worker/src/auth/canonical.ts`, `worker/src/auth/ecdsa.ts`):

1. **Hardware Key Wrapping**: On Android, `KeyVault.kt` creates a non-exportable AES-256-GCM key inside `AndroidKeyStore` and wraps the handset's P-256 private key before storing it in local libSQL as `keystore:v1:<iv>:<ciphertext>`. D1 stores only the public key. Exfiltrating either database cannot impersonate the handset.
2. **Canonical 5-Line String**:
   ```text
   METHOD
   PATH
   TIMESTAMP
   NONCE
   SHA256(raw_body_bytes)
   ```
   - Separated by `0x0A` (`\n`), **no trailing newline**, **no query string** (any query parameter on a signed device route fails with `400 unexpected_query`).
   - Empty bodies (e.g., `GET`) use SHA-256 of zero bytes (`e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`).
3. **Strict Header Grammar**:
   - `X-Device-Id`: `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{8,64}$`
   - `X-Timestamp`: `^\d{13}$` (UTC epoch ms, must be within ±300,000 ms of edge clock)
   - `X-Nonce`: `^[0-9a-f]{32}$` (16 random bytes, lowercase hex)
   - `X-Signature`: standard Base64 (`=` padded) of the 64-byte IEEE P1363 `r || s` signature
4. **Atomic Replay Guard**: `DeviceGateway` records every spent `X-Nonce` inside its SQLite storage for `NONCE_WINDOW_MS` (300,000 ms). A reused nonce returns `401 nonce_replay` before any write occurs.
5. **Cross-Language Test Vectors**: `test-support/protocol-vectors.json` is verified identically by the TypeScript harness, Rust `simulator/core`, and `test-support/independent-canonical-check.py`.

## Operator Authentication & Sessions

Registration is strictly **invite-only** (no public sign-up). Four sign-in factors are supported:
1. **Passkey (WebAuthn)** — primary, phishing-resistant; `AUTH_RP_ID` pinned to the deployment hostname.
2. **TOTP** — optional second factor (requires a passkey to enroll); disabling deletes the secret and clears all pending challenges.
3. **Password** — optional; defaults to `AUTH_PASSWORD_MODE=client-derived` (210,000-round PBKDF2 in the browser) to stay inside Workers Free 10 ms CPU limits.
4. **Magic Link** — advertised only when `RESEND_API_KEY` is configured; consumed exclusively via button `POST /v1/auth/magic-link/consume` so email scanners cannot burn links.

- **Host-only session cookies**: `__Secure-better-auth.session_token` (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, 7 days) is bound strictly to the Worker's origin—never open the console through a localhost reverse proxy.
- **Dual-scope lockout**: `AuthGuard` enforces 5 attempts/account and 20 attempts/IP per 900s window.

---

<!-- source: /docs/architecture/wasm-and-agent-isolation.md -->

# Wasm & Agent Isolation

> How DakFlare guarantees deterministic flow evaluation across Rust/Wasm runtimes and enforces fail-closed authority isolation for AI agents.

## Deterministic Single-Engine Flow Execution

Instead of maintaining separate JavaScript and Rust rule evaluators that inevitably drift, DakFlare compiles **one** pure-Rust crate (`simulator/flow`) to three targets:
1. **Android Handset** (`simulator/core` native Rust) — offline synchronous evaluation.
2. **Cloudflare Worker** (`worker/src/wasm/flow.wasm`) — fallback & continuation past `delay`/`webhook` nodes.
3. **Browser Console** (`dashboard/static/flow.wasm`) — instant simulation & regex synthesis in `/admin/workflows/edit`.

### Pure Evaluation, Caller-Owned Effects

The Wasm module imports **zero host functions** (`WebAssembly.instantiate(flowModule, {})`). It cannot make network calls, read clocks, or touch storage. It receives `{ graph, message }` and returns a pure list of `FlowAction` intents (`send_sms`, `delay`, `webhook`). The host enforces all side-effect safety:
- `webhook` URLs are validated as `https://` and SSRF-guarded against loopback, RFC 1918 private ranges, CGNAT, and cloud metadata IPs before enqueueing on `WEBHOOK_QUEUE`.
- `delay` steps >5 seconds hand off to durable `FlowExecutionWorkflow` checkpoints.

## Fail-Closed Agent Isolation

1. **Closed-Set System 1 vs. Prose Assistant**: `/v1/agent/*` uses Cloudflare Clef (`worker/src/lib/system1.ts`) to return typed probabilities (`choice`, `noul`, `score`) over closed sets—never free-form prose masquerading as telemetry. When unreachable, endpoints return less (`source: "unavailable"`) rather than hallucinating.
2. **Authority Cannot Self-Approve**: `createGrant` and `decideApproval` enforce `assertHuman(actor)`. Even if the `AssistantAgent` Durable Object imports them, it cannot mint its own grants.
3. **Effect-Shaped Grants & Fail-Closed Journaling**:
   - Every act in `AssistantAgent` writes a `tool_calls` row in SQLite *before* executing and derives its effect idempotency key from `call_id` (the LLM never picks idempotency keys).
   - Every act re-checks the live grant, autonomy window owner, per-window cap, and deployment-wide `daily_sms_cap` at call time.
   - Replayed tool calls return the recorded result (`replayed: true`) and refund grant uses so retries never burn `max_uses`.
4. **Schema Rollback Safety**: `AssistantAgent` maintains its own `schema_version` ledger inside `blockConcurrencyWhile` and fails closed with `503 agent_schema_ahead` if a Worker rollback encounters newer Durable Object SQLite state.

---

<!-- source: /docs/service-binding.md -->

# Service binding

> Call this deployment from another Worker or a Cloudflare Workflow as a typed service, and what a binding is allowed to do.

DakFlare exports a **`WorkerEntrypoint`** called `DakFlareApi`. A second Worker in the same
Cloudflare account — or a Cloudflare Workflow, which runs inside one — can bind this script as a
service and call typed methods instead of building a `Request` and remembering which header carries
the credential.

```ts
const sent = await env.DAKFLARE.sendSms({ to: "+15550169912", body: "Payment settled." });
const fleet = await env.DAKFLARE.devices();
const turn = await env.DAKFLARE.ask("How many rules are enabled?");
```

Every method delegates to the same router the public API uses. Scopes, rate limiters, audit rows,
idempotency and the D1 session bookmark behave exactly as they do for an HTTP caller — this is a
calling convention, not a second code path.

## The consumer's config

```toml
# the consumer Worker's wrangler.toml
[[services]]
binding = "DAKFLARE"
service = "dakflare-worker"
entrypoint = "DakFlareApi"
```

The consumer needs a compatibility date that supports RPC entrypoints; this repository's Worker runs
`compatibility_date = "2026-04-07"` with `nodejs_compat`, which is what the entrypoint is built and
tested against.

## Who may act

`BINDING_AUTH` on the **producer** decides, read per call so a deploy changes it without a warm
isolate holding the old answer:

| Mode | Credential | What a bound Worker can do |
|---|---|---|
| `trusted` (default) | none — the binding is the credential | everything the deployment can, including sending SMS and spending money |
| `agent_token` | a `dkf_agt_` token passed per call | whatever that token's scopes allow; an act additionally needs a live authority grant |

`trusted` is the default because a single-owner account is already the trust boundary, and it is
also why the limits below matter. If `BINDING_AUTH=trusted` and the deployment has no
`ADMIN_TOKEN`, every credentialed call refuses with `binding_untrusted` naming both ways out,
rather than running unauthenticated.

## What a binding cannot do

- **It cannot cross accounts.** Service bindings, queues, workflows and rate-limit namespaces are
  account-scoped. From another account, call the HTTP API with a `dkf_agt_` token.
- **A raw Durable Object binding bypasses all of it.** Binding `AssistantAgent` or `DeviceGateway`
  directly gives you their RPC methods with no session, no scope, no rate limit and no audit row —
  the binding is the authorisation. Use `DakFlareApi` unless you are deliberately operating the
  object.
- **It cannot see another machine's transcript by accident.** The entrypoint sends
  `X-Dakflare-Client: binding`, so its conversation and attachments are its own. `ADMIN_TOKEN`
  remains one shared credential: this separates cooperating clients by declared identity, not
  cryptographically.

## Where to go next

| | |
|---|---|
| [From a Worker](/docs/service-binding/worker) | the local interface, the calls, the error shape |
| [From a Cloudflare Workflow](/docs/service-binding/workflow) | `step.do`, the retry rule, and why the idempotency key is the whole safety story |
| [Method reference](/docs/service-binding/reference) | every method, its route, its arguments and its credential |

---

<!-- source: /docs/service-binding/worker.md -->

# From another Worker

> The typed calls, the local interface a consumer needs, the request() escape hatch, and how refusals arrive.

A Worker in the same account holds the binding in `env` and calls methods on it. There is nothing to
authenticate by hand in `trusted` mode, and nothing to serialise: arguments and results are
structured-clone values, not JSON strings.

## The interface a consumer needs

`dakflare-worker` is not published to npm, so there is no type to import. Declare the part you call,
and keep `worker/src/binding-api.ts` as the reference when a method changes:

```ts
// the consumer's types.ts
export interface DakFlareBinding {
  health(): Promise<unknown>;
  deployment(): Promise<unknown>;
  devices(): Promise<unknown>;
  messages(query?: { limit?: number; deviceId?: string; direction?: string }): Promise<unknown>;
  sendSms(
    input: { to: string; body: string; deviceId?: string; idempotencyKey?: string },
    options?: { token?: string }
  ): Promise<unknown>;
  ask(
    message: string,
    options?: { idempotencyKey?: string; token?: string }
  ): Promise<unknown>;
  request(
    input: {
      path: string;
      method?: string;
      body?: unknown;
      headers?: Record<string, string>;
      token?: string;
    },
    needsCredential?: boolean
  ): Promise<{ status: number; body: unknown; bookmark: string | null }>;
}

interface Env {
  DAKFLARE: Service<DakFlareBinding>;
}
```

The `token` fields matter only in `agent_token` mode; leaving them out is what makes that mode
impossible to use, so they are part of the declaration rather than an afterthought.

## Sending something

```ts
export default {
  async fetch(request: Request, env: Env): Promise<Response> {
    const { to, body } = await request.json<{ to: string; body: string }>();

    // Idempotent by key: the same key returns the same command instead of a second SMS.
    const sent = await env.DAKFLARE.sendSms({
      to,
      body,
      idempotencyKey: request.headers.get("idempotency-key") ?? undefined,
    });

    return Response.json(sent);
  },
};
```

In `agent_token` mode the same call carries the credential:

```ts
await env.DAKFLARE.sendSms({ to, body }, { token: env.DAKFLARE_AGENT_TOKEN });
```

## Reaching a route the shortcuts do not cover

`request()` is the escape hatch over everything under `/v1`, with the same authentication rules.
A route added to the HTTP API is callable the day it ships, which is what keeps the two surfaces
from drifting:

```ts
const saved = await env.DAKFLARE.request({
  path: "/v1/admin/workflows/wf_bkash",
  method: "PUT",
  body: { name: "bKash receipts", enabled: true, graph },
});
```

`request()` returns the status instead of throwing on 2xx; a 4xx or 5xx is refused the same way the
shortcuts are.

## Refusals

A failure is a thrown error carrying a code, a status and the route's own sentence. Branch on the
code, never on the message:

```ts
try {
  await env.DAKFLARE.sendSms({ to, body });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof Error && "code" in error) {
    // binding_untrusted      · trusted mode with no ADMIN_TOKEN on the deployment
    // binding_token_required · agent_token mode and no token was passed
    // idempotency_conflict   · the key is bound to a different message
    // turn_in_progress       · another turn holds that key right now
    // sms_cap / write_cap    · the window's ceiling is spent
  }
  throw error;
}
```

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `binding_untrusted` | `trusted` mode, but the deployment has no `ADMIN_TOKEN` to act as |
| `binding_token_required` | `agent_token` mode, and the call passed no token |
| `idempotency_conflict` | that key already answered a different message |
| `turn_in_progress` | another turn is running under this key |
| `sms_cap` / `write_cap` / `daily_sms_cap` | the autonomy ceiling is spent |
| the route's own code | anything the HTTP API would have returned |

Next: [from a Cloudflare Workflow](/docs/service-binding/workflow), where a retrying step makes the
idempotency key load-bearing.

---

<!-- source: /docs/service-binding/workflow.md -->

# From a Cloudflare Workflow

> Use the binding inside a Workflow step, and the one rule that makes a retrying step safe.

A Workflow is a class in a Worker. It receives the same `env`, so the binding is used exactly as it
is from a Worker — inside `step.do`, where the platform may run it more than once.

```ts
import { WorkflowEntrypoint, type WorkflowEvent, type WorkflowStep } from "cloudflare:workers";

interface Payload {
  to: string;
  invoice: string;
}

export class InvoiceFollowUp extends WorkflowEntrypoint<Env, Payload> {
  async run(event: WorkflowEvent<Payload>, step: WorkflowStep) {
    const { to, invoice } = event.payload;

    const first = await step.do("first notice", async () =>
      this.env.DAKFLARE.sendSms({
        to,
        body: `Invoice ${invoice} is due.`,
        // A step retries. The key is what makes the retry a replay instead of a second SMS.
        idempotencyKey: `invoice-${invoice}-notice-1`,
      }),
    );

    await step.sleep("wait three days", "3 days");

    await step.do("second notice", async () =>
      this.env.DAKFLARE.sendSms({
        to,
        body: `Invoice ${invoice} is still due.`,
        idempotencyKey: `invoice-${invoice}-notice-2`,
      }),
    );

    return first;
  }
}
```

Export the class (`exports.workflow({ name: "invoice-follow-up" })` in `cloudflare.config.ts`, or the
equivalent `workflows` entry in `wrangler.toml`) and `cf deploy` attaches it. The consumer's service
binding is declared exactly as in [the overview](/docs/service-binding):

```toml
[[services]]
binding = "DAKFLARE"
service = "dakflare-worker"
entrypoint = "DakFlareApi"

[[workflows]]
name = "invoice-follow-up"
binding = "INVOICE_FOLLOW_UP"
class_name = "InvoiceFollowUp"
```

## The two rules that make it safe

1. **Every `step.do` can run more than once.** Derive the `idempotencyKey` from the event and the
   step's purpose — never from `Date.now()`, a random value, or the step's attempt number. A key that
   changes on retry buys a second SMS.
2. **A step's result is durable; its side effect is not.** If a step sends and then fails before
   returning, the retry re-enters the closure. The key is what turns that into a no-op: the second
   `sendSms` with the same key returns the recorded command.

A step that runs out of retries is what `step.do` reports; it does not retry forever. If a notice
must not be missed, put the ceiling in the workflow (`retries: { limit: 5, delay: "30 seconds" }`)
and let a failed workflow be visible rather than silently swallowed.

## `step.sleep` is not the flow interpreter's `delay`

They look similar and are not:

| | Runs where | After a restart | Reported as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `step.sleep` | Cloudflare's Workflow engine | resumes at the same step | durable |
| a `delay` node in a `dakflare.flow/v2` graph | the handset | depends on the phone | the run reports `partial`, and the Worker runs the rest |

A flow the handset could only partly perform says so, and the Worker executes the actions after that
boundary — the state-machine reference has the exact rule. Use `step.sleep` for orchestration you
control; use a flow `delay` when the phone must act while the gateway is unreachable.

## This repository's own Workflow

`flow-execution-workflow` (bound here as `FLOW_WORKFLOW`, class `FlowExecutionWorkflow`) is the
Worker's own delay and webhook runner. A consumer can bind it, but its event payload is internal:
it is invoked by the flow fallback, and its shape is not a contract. Bind `DakFlareApi` instead.

---

<!-- source: /docs/service-binding/reference.md -->

# Method reference

> Every DakFlareApi method, the route it reaches, its arguments and whether it needs a credential.

Every method delegates to `handleFetch`, the router the public API uses. The "route" column is what
an HTTP caller would have hit; the "credential" column is whether `agent_token` mode requires a
token for that call in `trusted` mode it never does.

| Method | Route | Credential |
|---|---|---|
| `health()` | `GET /v1/auth/mode` | none — public by design |
| `deployment()` | `GET /v1/admin/health` | yes |
| `devices()` | `GET /v1/devices` | yes |
| `messages({ limit, deviceId, direction })` | `GET /v1/messages` | yes |
| `sendSms(input, options?)` | `POST /v1/sms/send` | yes |
| `ask(message, options?)` | `POST /v1/admin/agent/say` | yes |
| `request(input, needsCredential?)` | anything under `/v1` | yes, unless `false` is passed |

## `health()`

Liveness and the deployment's auth mode. The one call that needs no credential, so a bound Worker can
check the service without holding `ADMIN_TOKEN`.

Returns the `/v1/auth/mode` document: `auth_mode`, `auth_configured`, `password_mode`, `magic_link`.

## `deployment()`

The operator's own health read: device, message, rule and alert counts, and the checks the Overview
shows. Same document the console's overview consumes.

## `devices()`

The paired fleet with each device's label, presence and last-seen stamp.

## `messages({ limit, deviceId, direction })`

The message log, newest first.

| Argument | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | number | the route clamps it; omit for the default |
| `deviceId` | string | one handset |
| `direction` | `"in"` or `"out"` | omit for both |

Rows carry `channel`, `conversation_id`, `session_state` and `window_expires_at` when the row belongs
to a conversation, which is what tells you whether a free-form reply is allowed.

## `sendSms(input, options?)`

| Argument | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `to` | string | E.164 |
| `body` | string | the message text |
| `deviceId` | string, optional | omit to let the deployment choose |
| `idempotencyKey` | string, optional | 8–64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -`; the same key returns the same command |
| `options.token` | string, optional | required in `agent_token` mode |

Returns `{ command_id, replayed, lifecycle }`. `command_id` is what `status` reads; `lifecycle` is the
canonical state (see the state-machine reference). **`SENT` is not delivery** — `DELIVERED` requires a
status report from the handset.

## `ask(message, options?)`

| Argument | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `message` | string | one question for the agent |
| `options.idempotencyKey` | string, optional | a retry replays the recorded answer |
| `options.token` | string, optional | required in `agent_token` mode |

Returns the turn: the answer, any proposals the agent prepared, and `replayed` when the key had
already been answered. Reusing a key with different text is a refusal (`idempotency_conflict`), not a
silent replay.

## `request(input, needsCredential?)`

The escape hatch. `input.path` is everything after the origin, e.g. `/v1/admin/workflows/wf_bkash`;
`method` defaults to `GET`; `body` is serialised for you; `headers` are added to the ones the
entrypoint sets.

Returns `{ status, body, bookmark }`, where `body` is parsed JSON when the route answered JSON and the
text otherwise. `bookmark` is the D1 session bookmark when the route returned one, which lets a caller
chain a read-your-writes sequence.

Passing `false` as the second argument skips the credential — only for routes that are public by
design, and it is shown here so the option is not a mystery.

## What is not exposed

- **No Durable Object methods.** Binding a class directly skips every gate; the entrypoint exists so
  you do not have to.
- **No cross-account calls.** A binding is account-scoped; another account uses the HTTP API with a
  `dkf_agt_` token.
- **No streaming.** A conversation turn over the socket (`/agents/*`) is a browser surface; `ask`
  returns the finished turn.

---

<!-- source: /docs/agents.md -->

# Docs for Agents

> Machine-readable endpoints, llms.txt indexes, per-page Markdown content negotiation, OpenAPI 3.1, SKILL.md, and the Docs MCP server for AI coding agents.

DakFlare treats AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, OpenCode, and autonomous workflows) as a first-class audience served from the same source of truth as the human documentation.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints

| Endpoint | Format | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`/llms.txt`](/llms.txt) | Markdown index | Concise navigation index ordered by onboarding priority with one-line descriptions |
| [`/llms-full.txt`](/llms-full.txt) | Concatenated Markdown | Complete documentation bundle with `llms-ignore` JSX stripped and `llms-only` context preserved |
| `/docs/{any-path}.md` | `text/markdown; charset=utf-8` | Clean source Markdown for any page (e.g. `/docs/start/quickstart.md`, `/docs/reference/api-reference.md`) |
| `Accept: text/markdown` | HTTP content negotiation | Any doc URL returns clean Markdown with `Vary: Accept` and `x-markdown-tokens` budget header |
| [`/openapi.json`](/openapi.json) | OpenAPI 3.1.0 JSON | The 17 operations the API playground covers (pairing, poll, status, send, devices, messages, one workflow route, the four `/v1/agent/*` endpoints, webhooks, health, auth mode, `/mcp`), with security schemes, request/response examples, and error shapes |
| [`/SKILL.md`](/SKILL.md) | Agent Skill Markdown | Curated single-file skill encoding DakFlare invariants, CLI rules, Wasm ABI, and Do/Don't guardrails |
| [`/AGENTS.md`](/AGENTS.md) | Repository Agent Guide | Repo-root instructions for coding agents working directly inside `dakflare` |
| `POST /mcp` | JSON-RPC 2.0 (Docs MCP) | Live retrieval tools: `list_sections`, `search_docs`, `get_doc_page`, `get_openapi_operation` |

## Fetching Markdown Directly

```bash
# Via explicit .md route
curl -sS https://docs.dakflare.dev/docs/start/quickstart.md

# Via HTTP content negotiation (returns x-markdown-tokens header)
curl -i -H "Accept: text/markdown" https://docs.dakflare.dev/docs/reference/mcp-tools/
```

## Querying the Docs MCP Server

```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://docs.dakflare.dev/mcp \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"get_openapi_operation","arguments":{"path":"/v1/sms/send"}}}'
```

## Installing DakFlare's Task-Specific Skills

In addition to the unified [`/SKILL.md`](/SKILL.md), the repository ships four modular skills under `skills/` compatible with `npx skills add`:
- `skills/dakflare-provision/SKILL.md` — install, deploy, repair, pair, revoke
- `skills/dakflare-messaging/SKILL.md` — async send, idempotency, delivery status
- `skills/dakflare-flows/SKILL.md` — `dakflare.flow/v2` authoring, validation, drift healing
- `skills/dakflare-agents/SKILL.md` — `dkf_agt_` tokens, grants, approvals, `/mcp`
